1000.author: yuanzhou75
1000.body:
## Context

Split from #439 (closed). The two non-UI asks from that issue are already done: unbuffered long-running launches (#611) and the agent documentation (`skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`). The remaining ask is tracked here.

## What's wanted

The session/job UI should show a process-level heartbeat for long-running work — live CPU, RSS, and last-output time — rather than relying on log-file mtime (or a quiet log) alone. Today a long job whose output is block-buffered looks stuck even while the process is busy.

## Scope / approach

TBD — the UI interaction still needs to be decided: where the telemetry lives, what granularity, how often it samples. Design to be confirmed before implementation.

Related: #434, #439.
1000.title: [Feature]Process-level heartbeat (CPU / RSS / last-output) in the session/job UI

1006.author: HongyeZhou
1006.body:
## What happens

The `Binary release (x86_64)` job fails at the very last step, after the artifact is built successfully:

```
Built /home/runner/work/sciencediscovery/sciencediscovery/dist/binary-release/ScienceDiscovery-d255bc9-linux-x86_64 (696.9 MiB, payload f381e6e7b55448e4f127d6fef344dc30)
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

Two occurrences today, both in merge-queue runs for a PR that does not touch packaging (PR #999, which changes `apps/desktop` + `services/api` export saving):

| run | head | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [42491940459](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42491940459) | `fa9878e` | failed, same line |
| [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) | `1c585656` | failed, same line |

The same job passed minutes earlier and later on sibling queue runs ([42505053918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42505053918) for #1004, [42496441065](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42496441065) for #992), so it is intermittent rather than tied to a head.

Both times the payload scan before it passed: `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found.`

## Why this looks like the gate's own false positive

The gate is `assert_no_release_build_paths()` in `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:94-112`. It greps the whole single-file artifact for `$repository_root`, `$output_dir`, `$HOME` and `$USERPROFILE`. On a GitHub-hosted runner `$HOME` is `/home/runner`.

The payload inside that artifact has already been checked by `assert_no_build_paths()` in `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh:144-191`, which deliberately allows two things the artifact-level check cannot:

1. For the `$HOME` needle it excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` (that dependency closure legitimately mentions `/home/runner`).
2. It passes two supplier SBOMs through `scripts/binary-release/filter-upstream-sbom-paths.mjs`, because `pydantic_core-*.dist-info/sboms/pydantic-core.cyclonedx.json` and `watchfiles-*.dist-info/sboms/watchfiles_rust_notify.cyclonedx.json` carry upstream references of the form `path+file:///home/runner/work/pydantic/...` and `path+file:///home/runner/work/watchfiles/...`.

So the payload scan passing tells us the only `/home/runner` occurrences in the payload are the ones it has already ruled acceptable. The artifact-level scan then re-checks those same bytes with no allowance and no way to exclude a subtree, and the only needle that can match is the generic `$HOME` — a bare `/home/runner`, not this build's repository root.

Intermittency fits the layout: the artifact is the pinned `node` binary plus an injected SEA blob plus a `tar | zstd` payload plus a 48-byte footer (`scripts/binary-release/build-binary.mjs:232-262`), so the approved SBOM bytes only appear verbatim when zstd emits that region as a stored block.

## Impact

It blocks the merge queue for PRs that never touch packaging, and each occurrence costs a full payload build (about 9 minutes) plus a queue round-trip. #999 has been kicked out twice today; `merge-gate` goes red as collateral.

## Suggested fix

- Keep the artifact-level check for the build-specific needles only (`$repository_root`, `$output_dir`) — a match there cannot be an upstream coincidence — and drop `$HOME`/`$USERPROFILE` from it, since `build-payload.sh` already covers those with the allowances that a single compressed blob cannot apply.
- Or run the artifact-level check against the decompressed payload (the `--keep-payload` tree) so the SBOM filter can apply to it as well.
- Worth a case in the existing `scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs` suite: a payload whose only `/home/runner` hits are the two approved SBOM references must pass both checks.

To confirm locally: build with `--keep-payload` and grep the payload tree for `/home/runner`; the hits should be exactly those two SBOMs plus anything under `jiuwenswarm/` or `adapter/`.
1006.title: [Bug] Binary release gate fails on the generic $HOME needle (/home/runner) the payload scan already allows

1007.author: HongyeZhou
1007.body:
## What happens

The `UT` job fails intermittently with one test short of the plan, always in the same place:

```
- ut: status FAIL
- ut: passed 6939 of 6940 planned
- ut: 1 failed
- ut: NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1
- ut: NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: services/api/src/server.test.ts
- ut: FAIL: services/api/src/server.test.ts::updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password@linux/amd64
```

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` has already logged `Done 512/605: services/api/src/server.test.ts (180712ms)` earlier in the same run, so the failure is not at an assertion in the test body: it is the file's teardown.

## Occurrences

Four times in one afternoon, on three unrelated PRs, every one of them a different head:

| PR | run | attempt | UT job | named test | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #999 | [42487399804](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804) (merge queue) | 1 | [128752365509](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804/job/128752365509) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6909/6910 |
| #734 | [42482149231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231) | 1 | [128736356154](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231/job/128736356154) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6939/6940 |
| #1004 | [42485316924](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924) | 1 | [128745961451](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924/job/128745961451) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6906/6907 |
| #999 | [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) (merge queue) | 1 | [128800209585](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754/job/128800209585) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6935/6936 |

`#734` attempt 2 and `#1004` attempt 2, on the same commits, passed. Two of the four blocked the merge queue (`merge-gate` goes red as collateral), so each one costs a queue round-trip plus a nine-minute payload/CI re-run.

## Why this is the harness, not the PR under test

- `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` is emitted only for a `test:fail` event that carries no per-test token — a file-scope hook or a collection failure, by construction: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:128`.
- `NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1` means the `node --test` worker process for that file exited non-zero: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:195`. So the process died, and the "1 failed" test is the plan's attribution of that, not a failed expectation.
- The named test changes between runs while the file is byte-identical, which a genuine assertion failure in one specific case would not do.
- The four runs span three PRs whose diffs never touch `services/api/src/server.test.ts`, the SSH credential path or the workspace writer path: #734 is configuration capabilities, #1004 is shell-execution settlement, #999 is desktop/API export saving.
- Every occurrence passes on a plain re-run of the same commit.

## Suggested fix

- `server.test.ts` registers many teardown hooks as `context.after(() => new Promise((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve())))` (`:868`, `:872`, `:2578`, `:2582`, `:1933`, ...). `server.close()`'s callback does not fire while an idle keep-alive client socket is still open, so such a hook can hang and take the worker down with it. The file already has the shared `closeApiServer()` helper (`:152`, `:160`) that the rest of the file uses; those hooks should use it too, or pair each `close()` with `closeAllConnections()` the way `:591` does for the adapter.
- The two named tests both start a probe against a stub server. Ending that probe explicitly in the test's own `after` hook, and awaiting it, removes the most likely lingering handle.
- Give the hooks a timeout so a stuck teardown reports the hook and the file by name, instead of surfacing as a worker exit with no reason attached.
- Complementary: have the coordinator include the worker's exit code and signal in the `NODE_WORKER_FAILED` annotation. Right now the only thing a reader gets is `worker-1`, which is what makes every occurrence cost a manual log dig.

Reported from PR review triage; not tied to any single PR.
1007.title: [Bug] UT flakes at server.test.ts teardown: NODE_WORKER_FAILED worker-1 + NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED, 1 of ~6900 failed
